closure_unit.outcome: Only the current authorized claimant/attempt can make a legal atomic microtask transition; stale and duplicate actors cannot corrupt successor or terminal state.

materialized_acceptance.requirement: Inventory every authoritative job mutation in the owning queue/executor/outcome/cancellation paths and narrow production adapter. Claim creation binds the winning claimant and attempt/generation to canonical authority. Subsequent running, completion, failure, requeue, escalation, hard-gate and cancellation transitions require the matching current claimant/attempt/generation and expected prior state. No public or internal job-id-only mutation bypass remains; authorized system transitions use their existing explicit authority.

The canonical SurrealDB mutation checks the full current authority and transition preconditions in one atomic operation. With two real independent clients against the same Handshake-managed canonical store, A claims, A expires or is explicitly superseded, and B owns the next attempt. Every stale A attempt to mark running, complete, fail or requeue is denied without changing B's job, outcome, receipt or lease. A shared in-process mutex, fake RecordingIo or query-text assertion cannot satisfy this proof.

An authorized duplicate completion with the same bound operation identity/payload returns its canonical outcome or a deterministic already-completed result without a second transition. Conflicting retry, stale generation, changed payload/context and illegal prior state cannot overwrite, reopen or relabel a terminal job. Canonical commit/receipt reconciliation handles outcome-unknown acknowledgement before retry; no new lease system.

Preserve the existing atomic queued-state claim, FairScheduler priority/fairness behavior and durable starvation watermark. Two independent concurrent claimers cannot both own the same attempt. A denied stale mutation does not consume B's claim, advance the watermark incorrectly, starve unrelated eligible work or destroy historical claim provenance.

The production SurrealMtExecutorIo propagates the actual ExecutorIdentity and current existing lease/attempt evidence into transitions instead of discarding it. Expired/revoked session/grant/claim authority, wrong account/Principal/AccessSpace/workspace and a context switch fail closed at mutation commit. Read-only mailbox, navigation or DCC projections cannot mint or extend claim authority.

Active, failed, cancelled, never-started and outcome-unknown states remain distinct in canonical results and projections. Lease expiry/revocation is not fabricated completion, failure, cancellation or STOP. Preserve accepted terminal outcomes, partial results and original run/attempt attribution; late worker messages cannot change a successor or terminal state.

Accepted business transitions and rejected stale attempts have scoped typed results and canonical Flight Recorder/EventLedger linkage where required. internal_diagnostics records bounded claimant-generation/transition disposition and unknown state without private payloads. Existing passive Palmistry independently retains permitted operational evidence and performs no retries/recovery. Update the same-change UserManual, publish the typed contract for MT-209 display/actions and prove account/revocation negatives without metadata leaks.

risks.risk: A stale A completes after B takes ownership.
risks.control: Atomic current claimant, attempt/generation and prior-state predicates with two real independent clients and canonical reread.

risks.risk: Duplicate completion rewrites terminal state or emits a second durable outcome.
risks.control: Bind idempotency to context, payload and preconditions; reconcile the canonical receipt and reject conflicting retry.

risks.risk: A lease check races revocation before the mutation.
risks.control: Check current authenticated authority at the commit boundary under existing lease/storage owners; test concurrent expiry and revocation.

risks.risk: Fencing changes break fairness, watermark durability or unrelated work.
risks.control: Retain current scheduler/claim/watermark targets and include permitted unrelated work while a stale actor is denied.

risks.risk: Expired or unknown work is displayed as completed/cancelled.
risks.control: Preserve explicit lifecycle distinctions and pair MT-209 projections with canonical reads and scoped diagnostic evidence.

specification_anchor_refs.anchor: 2.6.8.10.3.3 Role Mailbox executor routing, claim-or-lease semantics, and response authority
specification_anchor_refs.requirement: Current claimant, claim identity, expiry, takeover and response authority remain distinct from read visibility; expiry does not imply completion or cancellation.

specification_anchor_refs.anchor: Authoritative control-plane records; software-delivery Dev Command Center projection requirements
specification_anchor_refs.requirement: SurrealDB/EventLedger owns queue/claim state. DCC and mailbox projections cannot authorize linked-state mutation.
Reuse current shared-owner epoch fencing, reauthorization, precondition-bound idempotency and accepted-outcome reconciliation where applicable. No second plugin/lease platform.

source_evidence.observed: FairScheduler atomically claims a queued row and records session/time. Ranking is separate; the guarded write prevents double claim.
StarvationGuard uses a durable atomic watermark. Preserve it rather than replacing fairness or claiming the scheduler is absent.
UPDATE_STATE_QUERY and update_state take job_id, target state and reason, without claimant, attempt/generation or expected prior-state predicates. The hard_gated guard is not a claimant fence.
SurrealMtExecutorIo::mark_running discards _executor_identity and calls queue.update_state by job_id.
The adapter already uses mailbox executor routing and acquire/takeover lease methods. Reuse its current authority rather than adding another lease system.
Existing job states and claimed_by_session/claimed_at_utc are explicit; preserve their semantics and bind missing mutation preconditions in the owning contract.
Existing targets cover guarded claims, priority/fairness and watermark behavior. Current authoring made no runtime claim.
Existing integration target imports the production SurrealMtExecutorIo, executor identity and RoleMailboxClaimLeaseV1; some tests use RecordingIo, which cannot prove canonical storage atomicity.

module_contract.boundary_change: Extend the existing owner's typed contract and narrowly bind existing callers; no second scheduler, quota/lease authority or aggregate crate.
module_contract.dependency_direction: Production adapters and native projections consume the owning module's typed contract. The module does not depend on native GUI or Palmistry implementation.
module_contract.build_unit_policy: Keep small focused logical modules or existing independently selectable crates. No giant aggregate crate, arbitrary numeric build cap, compulsory crate split or blanket refactor.
module_contract.canonical_source: Existing WP-declared Product source under the preserved active pin. This contract does not repin or publish reusable source.

adapter_paths.scope: Only MtExecutorIo/SurrealMtExecutorIo propagation of current executor/lease/attempt evidence into the mt_executor command contract and affected result mapping; preserve process-ledger ownership.
Only microtask mutation/claim/recovery guidance through the existing UserManual producer and its canonical version; exact entry binding at allocation, no new manual system.
Only affected command/navigation/manual registration; read visibility never implies mutation authority.

module_contract.shared_binding_policy: Only exact named adapter slices may change after owner allocation; ownership stays with the existing module and physical custodian.

public_contract.change: Publish a typed mutation precondition from the existing claimant/lease authority with job identity, claimant, execution attempt/generation, current authorization and expected prior state. Return a scoped applied/already-applied/conflict/denied/unknown disposition; exact type names follow the owning implementation.
inputs: Requested transition with expected prior state and stable operation identity
outputs: Atomically accepted transition and linked receipt
Unchanged canonical successor/terminal record on rejected mutation
public_contract.no_new_authority: A read projection, stale lease copy, mailbox message, caller-supplied generation or fixture is not proof of current authority.
